name: Newton's second law
description: Force equals mass times acceleration, the basic equation of motion for classical bodies.

name: newton's second law
description: Force equals mass times acceleration, the basic equation of motion for classical bodies.

name: Conservation of energy
description: The total energy of an isolated system stays constant, though it can change form.

name: Conservation of momentum
description: The total momentum of an isolated system stays constant, a result of translation symmetry.

name: Lagrangian mechanics
description: Reformulates mechanics using the difference between kinetic and potential energy and the principle of least action.

name: Hamiltonian mechanics
description: Describes a system through its total energy as a function of position and momentum.

name: Noether's theorem
description: Every continuous symmetry of a physical system corresponds to a conserved quantity.

name: Harmonic oscillator
description: A system pulled back toward equilibrium by a force proportional to displacement, oscillating at a natural frequency.

name: Maxwell's equations
description: Four equations describing how electric and magnetic fields are produced by charges and currents and how they change.

name: Lorentz force
description: The force on a charged particle moving through electric and magnetic fields.

name: Electromagnetic wave
description: A self-propagating oscillation of electric and magnetic fields that travels at the speed of light.

name: Faraday's law
description: A changing magnetic field induces an electric field around a closed loop.

name: Speed of light
description: The constant speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum, the same for all observers.

name: Special relativity
description: Space and time combine into spacetime, and the speed of light is the same in every inertial frame.

name: General relativity
description: Gravity is the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.

name: Time dilation
description: A moving clock runs slower than one at rest, as measured by the observer at rest.

name: Mass-energy equivalence
description: Mass and energy are interchangeable, expressed by E equals m c squared.

name: Black hole
description: A region where gravity is so strong that nothing, including light, can escape past the event horizon.

name: Gravitational wave
description: A ripple in spacetime produced by accelerating masses, first detected from merging black holes.

name: Schrodinger equation
description: The equation that governs how a quantum wave function changes over time.

name: Wave function
description: The mathematical description of a quantum state, whose squared size gives measurement probabilities.

name: Uncertainty principle
description: Position and momentum cannot both be known exactly at the same time.

name: Quantum tunneling
description: A particle can pass through an energy barrier that it could not cross classically.

name: Photon
description: The quantum of the electromagnetic field, a massless particle of light.

name: Photoelectric effect
description: Light above a threshold frequency ejects electrons from a metal, showing that light comes in quanta.

name: Quantum entanglement
description: Particles share a joint state so that measurement results are correlated even at a distance.

name: Spin
description: An intrinsic form of angular momentum carried by quantum particles.

name: Pauli exclusion principle
description: Two identical fermions cannot occupy the same quantum state.

name: Entropy
description: A measure of the number of microscopic arrangements of a system, which never decreases in an isolated system.

name: Second law of thermodynamics
description: The entropy of an isolated system does not decrease over time.

name: Boltzmann distribution
description: Gives the probability of a state in thermal equilibrium based on its energy and the temperature.

name: Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution
description: The distribution of particle speeds in an ideal gas at thermal equilibrium.

name: Plasma
description: An ionized gas of free electrons and ions whose behavior is dominated by collective electromagnetic forces.

name: Debye length
description: The distance over which a charge is screened by surrounding charges in a plasma.

name: Plasma frequency
description: The natural oscillation frequency of electrons in a plasma.

name: Particle-in-Cell method
description: A simulation method that moves particles through fields computed on a grid.

name: Magnetic reconnection
description: Magnetic field lines break and rejoin, rapidly converting magnetic energy into particle energy.

name: Nuclear fusion
description: Light nuclei combine into heavier ones and release energy, the process that powers stars.

name: Tokamak
description: A donut-shaped device that confines hot plasma with magnetic fields for fusion.

name: Neutron star
description: The dense remnant of a collapsed star, held up by neutron degeneracy pressure.
